newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine bonds slightly higher, slow session.
newsitem.headline: Argentine bonds slightly higher, slow session.

text.p: Argentine bonds were slightly higher late Tuesday after a slow session watching the U.S. Federal Reserve for signs on rates.
"Everybody is waiting for the Fed," said a trader at a local bank.
The Federal Reserve's Open Market Committee started its two-day policy-setting meeting Tuesday, but monetary policy is widely seen unchanged.
Argentina's FRB Brady bond due 2005 rose 1/8 to 90-3/8, while the dollar denominated Bocon Previsional 2 due 2001 rose $0.02 to 126.10.
Another trader said the market continued to look very firm, despite many players' recent forecast of a correction after the near consistent gains of January.

"My hope is that there is a correction, but if you sell now you're going to lose," said the trader. The main factors that continue to fuel the rally are high liquidity levels locally and abroad, say traders.
In the money markets, call money rates rose to 5.25 percent from 5.15 percent.
